picks.reasoning: The region rule decides this: LPL has beaten LEC 4-2 in 2026 and sits at 64% against other regions versus LEC's 50%, so AL's league is the stronger one. KC's 9-2 Worlds run and the 2-0 win over AL at EWC are the crowd's favourite story, and I don't buy it enough to pick against the region data.

KC owns the early tempo on paper (+1.4k at 15 at Worlds, 65% first blood and first tower) and beat AL 2-0 in July, but the LPL went 4-2 against the LEC this year and the region-strength rule says that carries more weight than a stat edge, so I'm backing AL to win this one.

LPL has the stronger international record here (9-5 against other regions, 4-2 over LEC this year), and the region rule weighs that heavily, so I'm backing AL despite KC's 2-0 win at EWC. KC's deeper pools and Caliste's form keep this close, and AL's draft will need to stay flexible to win it.

The house region rule carries the call: LPL beat LEC 4-2 in 2026 and wins 64% of international series against LEC's 50%. KC's numbers are stronger (+1.3k GD@15 against AL's -0.1k, plus a 9-2 Worlds run), so this is a lean, not a clear read.

KC has the better form and beat AL 2-0 at EWC, and their Worlds run is full of calm, connected play. But the LPL has the stronger international record, with a 4-2 edge over the LEC this year and all three Worlds titles to the LEC's zero, so I'll back AL to win this one. My concern is their mood: they've thrown leads and their last 20 games sit at 10-10, so I'd call this close.
